title: Mob lynching - is there a separate law or only general provisions
p1:
A crowd can become a weapon when anger replaces the rule of law.

But does India have a separate law that specifically deals with mob lynching?
p2:
Many people assume that mob lynching is covered by one dedicated nationwide law. The reality is more complex.

There is no separate central law exclusively defining and punishing mob lynching. Such cases are generally dealt with under existing criminal provisions related to murder, attempt to murder, rioting, unlawful assembly, and other offences depending on the facts of the case.

A key point many miss: being part of a violent mob does not always mean escaping responsibility by claiming you did not deliver the final blow. Members of an unlawful assembly can be held liable for acts committed by the group in certain circumstances.
p3:
Some states have introduced or proposed specific laws against mob lynching, while the broader criminal framework continues to apply across India.

The larger lesson is that law does not only look at the final act of violence; it also examines collective intent, participation, and the circumstances surrounding the offence.
conclusion: Should India have a separate nationwide law for mob lynching, or are existing criminal provisions enough to deal with such cases?
